corpus.name: 250k
corpus.note: The generator this repository started from, before it was made deterministic: the same messages, folders and seed as mailbench-v1, but dated from the day it was generated and with Spool-named MIME boundaries and one header. Close to mailbench-v1, and still a different mailbox: runs on the two do not go in one table.

source.note: Transcribed from Spool's benchmark page, where these runs were first published. The raw harness output is on the machine that measured them and has not been added to this repository yet; until it is, these are the only numbers here that CI cannot regenerate from the instrument's own lines.

calibration.note: As published with these results: one or two frames of the 60 Hz display, plus capture. The raw calibration was not kept with them.

mailflare.held: 300 messages at the start, 600 by the end
mailflare.note: Mailflare fetches only the newest 50 messages in each folder; scrolling the inbox during the tests made it fetch 300 more. The other clients held all 250,000.

thunderbird.note: Thunderbird keeps no offline copy of Junk and Trash by default. The rest of the mailbox it held in full.

notes.title: One client at a time.
notes.body: Each was the only mail client running while it was measured, after it had finished checking the server on launch.

notes.title: Idle CPU was taken straight after the tests.
notes.body: Apple Mail and Canary were both still working at that point — Apple Mail at a quarter of a core, Canary at more than one and a half — and the numbers say so rather than waiting until they stopped.

notes.title: Mailflare's next message is unexplained.
notes.body: Because it holds about the same few hundred messages at either size, its numbers here and at 50,000 differ by noise and by things not yet pinned down, not by scale: moving to the next message took 507 ms here against 273 ms at 50,000, and nobody yet knows why.

notes.title: Mailflare was measured later.
notes.body: On 30 October, on the same machine and the same server; the other five on 15 October.
